details.description: Llama 2 13B Chat is Meta's 13-billion-parameter fine-tuned version of Llama 2, tuned with supervised fine-tuning and RLHF for assistant-like dialogue in English. Released in July 2023 as part of the Llama 2 family (7B to 70B parameters), it builds on a base pretrained on 2 trillion tokens of publicly available data (knowledge cutoff September 2022) plus additional human-annotated data for instruction and safety tuning. Meta's own GitHub repository for Llama 2 is now marked deprecated, with development consolidated into newer repositories for later Llama generations.
advantages: Meta reports a 62.18% TruthfulQA score (informative-and-truthful responses) for the 13B chat model, per Meta's model card.
Meta reports 0.00% toxic generations on ToxiGen for the 13B chat model in its safety evaluation, per the model card.
Fine-tuned specifically for assistant-like dialogue rather than raw text completion.
Part of a family spanning 7B to 70B parameters trained with the same fine-tuning recipe, giving a range of compute/quality tradeoffs, per Meta's model card.
disadvantages: 4,096-token context window, per Meta's model card.
Officially supported for English only; Meta says other languages need developer fine-tuning and separate license compliance, per the model card.
Base training data has a knowledge cutoff of September 2022, per Meta's model card.
Meta's dedicated GitHub repository for Llama 2 is now marked deprecated, with development moved to newer repositories, per the repo's README.
use_cases: Assistant-style dialogue and conversational chat in English.
Base for further fine-tuning into domain-specific assistants.

sources.title: meta-llama/llama: Inference code for Llama models

notes: Catalog's 4,096-token max_input/max_output_tokens match Meta's stated 4K context window for Llama 2, so no conflict. The HF card's grouped academic-benchmark table (MMLU, BBH, etc.) is for the pretrained base sizes only, not the chat-tuned variant, so it was not reused here; only the fine-tuned safety table's TruthfulQA/ToxiGen numbers apply to this chat model. Meta's meta-llama/llama GitHub repo is itself marked deprecated in its README, with development consolidated into newer repos; that is about the repo/tooling, not a formal end-of-life notice for the model, and the catalog's deprecation_date is empty.
